# Numeric sequences

Running sums and scans, counting sequences, and an overflow-free midpoint.

<h2 id="partial-sum"><code>PartialSum&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func PartialSum<T>(
    items: T[..],
    into: var T[..]
) -> bool
```

Writes the running sums of `items` into `into`: element `i` becomes the sum of the first `i + 1` elements.
`into` may be `items` itself. Requires `+` on the element type, with whatever overflow it has.
Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Numeric.rux#L17)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type        | Description                                    |
| ------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `items` | `T[..]`     | the sequence to sum                            |
| `into`  | `var T[..]` | where the sums go, at least as long as `items` |

**Returns**: whether `into` was long enough; nothing is written when it was not

<h2 id="inclusive-scan"><code>InclusiveScan&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func InclusiveScan<T>(
    items: T[..],
    into: var T[..],
    combine: func(T, T) -> T
) -> bool
```

Writes the running combination of `items` into `into`: element `i` becomes the first `i + 1` elements combined
left to right with `combine`. [`PartialSum`](/docs/api/algorithms/numeric#partial-sum) is this scan with `+`.
`into` may be `items` itself.
Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing beyond whatever `combine` does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Numeric.rux#L41)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type              | Description                                       |
| --------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `items`   | `T[..]`           | the sequence to scan                              |
| `into`    | `var T[..]`       | where the results go, at least as long as `items` |
| `combine` | `func(T, T) -> T` | how two values combine                            |

**Returns**: whether `into` was long enough; nothing is written when it was not

<h2 id="exclusive-scan"><code>ExclusiveScan&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ExclusiveScan<T>(
    items: T[..],
    into: var T[..],
    initial: T,
    combine: func(T, T) -> T
) -> bool
```

Writes the running combination of `items` before each element into `into`: element `i` becomes `initial`
combined with the first `i` elements, so the first result is `initial` and the last element of `items` takes part
in none.
`into` may be `items` itself.
Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing beyond whatever `combine` does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Numeric.rux#L67)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type              | Description                                       |
| --------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `items`   | `T[..]`           | the sequence to scan                              |
| `into`    | `var T[..]`       | where the results go, at least as long as `items` |
| `initial` | `T`               | the value before anything is combined             |
| `combine` | `func(T, T) -> T` | how two values combine                            |

**Returns**: whether `into` was long enough; nothing is written when it was not

<h2 id="iota"><code>Iota&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Iota<T>(into: var T[..], start: T, step: T)
```

Fills `into` with `start`, `start + step`, `start + 2 * step` and so on.
Requires `+` on the element type, with whatever overflow it has.
Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Numeric.rux#L88)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type        | Description                            |
| ------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `into`  | `var T[..]` | the sequence to fill                   |
| `start` | `T`         | the first value                        |
| `step`  | `T`         | what each value adds to the one before |

<h2 id="midpoint"><code>Midpoint</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Midpoint(a: int64, b: int64) -> int64
pub func Midpoint(a: int32, b: int32) -> int32
pub func Midpoint(a: uint64, b: uint64) -> uint64
pub func Midpoint(a: uint32, b: uint32) -> uint32
pub func Midpoint(a: float64, b: float64) -> float64
```

Halfway between `a` and `b`, without overflowing to infinity when both are near the largest finite value.

| Overload                                               | Summary                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func Midpoint(a: int64, b: int64) -> int64`       | Halfway between `a` and `b`, rounded toward `a`, without overflowing however far apart they are.          |
| `pub func Midpoint(a: int32, b: int32) -> int32`       | Halfway between `a` and `b`, rounded toward `a`, without overflowing however far apart they are.          |
| `pub func Midpoint(a: uint64, b: uint64) -> uint64`    | Halfway between `a` and `b`, rounded toward `a`, without overflowing however far apart they are.          |
| `pub func Midpoint(a: uint32, b: uint32) -> uint32`    | Halfway between `a` and `b`, rounded toward `a`, without overflowing however far apart they are.          |
| `pub func Midpoint(a: float64, b: float64) -> float64` | Halfway between `a` and `b`, without overflowing to infinity when both are near the largest finite value. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Numeric.rux#L103)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                                                | Description   |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `a`  | `int64` / `int32` / `uint64` / `uint32` / `float64` | one end       |
| `b`  | `int64` / `int32` / `uint64` / `uint32` / `float64` | the other end |

**Returns**: the midpoint
